key_insight: AISPA introduces a user-centric way to audit hidden system prompts in AI applications, helping reveal how these prompts shape model behavior. The core breakthrough is making prompt governance more transparent and accountable without relying on developers to voluntarily disclose prompt contents.
problem_solved: Commercial AI systems often rely on system prompts that are not publicly shared, even though they strongly influence outputs, safety, and user experience. This creates a trust, compliance, and accountability gap for users, researchers, and regulators.
method: Defines a structured auditing framework, Artificial Intelligence System Prompt Assurance (AISPA), for inspecting system prompts from the user side.
Examines prompt-specific behaviors and responses to infer the presence and effects of hidden system instructions.
Provides a systematic process for evaluating whether AI applications behave consistently with stated policies, safety goals, and expected constraints.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, AISPA offers a practical path to test, monitor, and govern prompt-driven behaviors in deployed systems. It can improve transparency, support compliance efforts, and reduce the risk of undisclosed prompt-induced failures or policy violations.

paper_title: AISPA: User-Centric System Prompt Auditing for Large Language Model Applications
paper_authors: Xiangning Lin, Shenzhe Zhu, Shu Yang, Zhenyu Zhang, Haoqian Zhang
